notes: Every file control entry of an external report-file connector 'must have' the same OPTIONAL, consistent ASSIGN and RECORD DELIMITER, the same RESERVE, organization, access mode and 'The same specification for the PADDING CHARACTER clause' (§1985:XIII.2.3.4 GR1 a-g). ExternalFileConnectorRules#Check compares the entries of a compilation group by the one identity FileEntryIdentity#Segments (OPT, ASSIGN, DELIM, RESERVE, ORG, ACC, PAD, the omitted clause read as the implementor's value) and refuses a difference with COBOL6847 citing the 1985 rules; its FILE STATUS agreement arm is gated to 2023, so the 1985 freedom stands; the same identity is emitted (OoEmitter#EmitExternalDescribes) for the run-time ExternalTable#Describe comparison between separately compiled elements, which is a checking exception and off by default. Probes at 85 (outer program and contained INNERP both FD XR IS EXTERNAL REPORT IS ...): OPTIONAL, ASSIGN literal, RESERVE 2 vs 3 and vs omitted, PADDING "*" vs "#" and vs omitted, ORGANIZATION LINE SEQUENTIAL (also COBOL0900) and ACCESS DYNAMIC (also COBOL1858) each refused COBOL6847; PADDING data-names not external refused COBOL1624; identical entries, defaults vs written ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL/ACCESS SEQUENTIAL/RESERVE 1 AREA, STANDARD-1 vs omitted RECORD DELIMITER (the implementor's consistency rule, docs/CONFORMANCE.md) and different FILE STATUS items compile and run (OUTER OPEN 00 / INNER DONE / OUTER CLOSED 00). Separately compiled mismatching RESERVE runs undetected, which the rule permits (no result is specified for a nonconforming run unit). The witness runs two matching entries and prints INNER LINE 01.

next.reason: Items a-f carry over into §2023:12.4.5.3 GR1 a-f, with the implementor consistency rules documented per §2023:A.1 72 and §2023:A.1 149. But 1985 item g 'The same specification for the PADDING CHARACTER clause' is gone (2023 has no PADDING CHARACTER clause), and 2023 adds, for a report file's sequential FCE, 'i) The same specification of the FILE STATUS clause' (plus collating sequence, sharing and lock items). External report-file connectors that differ in FILE STATUS, legal in 1985, are now nonconforming.
